div.head: LATiA;sT NEWS.
div.p: LATiA;sT NEWS.

- _ Prince Ferdinand has decided to proceed to S, fia, and take the oath as Prince of Bulgaria. Lerd Clermort died on Friday afternoon at his seat etavensdale Park. near Newry. He was born in 1821. The "Standard" says Mr. Bright has agreed to take the chair at the Liberal Unionist dinner to Lord Halting- ten.
The fire at the naphtha springs at Baku are reported to !lave been extinguished after burning for four days, thereby derroying £2OOOOO worth of the fluid.

, PEIIPETUAL PENSIONS rho Select Committee on per- petual pensions have adapted their report, which declares gairist the principle of perpetual pensions, and condemns past commutations as having been na,de at too high a rate.

Sir George Trevelyan (GI) and Mr. Evelyn Ashley (UL) were nominated at Glasgow. oo Friday, for the vacancy in the representation of the Bridgeton Division. caused by the retirement of Mr. E. R. Russell (GL.) The polling is on Tuesday. THB ARREST OF MISS. CASs.—The "Pall Mall Gazette" save :—lt is stated that ?ir Charles Woman's report to the Home Secretary on the Cass inquiry entirely exonerates Miss Cass ef the charges brought against her by Police- constable Endacott, and leaves the whole question of future proceedings in relation to the policeman to Mr. Matthews.

A LADY ACCIDENTALLY POISONED.-11i8S Briggs, Of Crr‘rnpton Fold, Bolton, and daughter of the late Mr. Christopher Briggs, IP., was accidentally poisoned on Fri- day. She has, it appears, been under medical treatment for some time, and on seeing her medical adviser, Dr. Gilli- brand, on Thursday, that gentleman prescribed some medi- cine. The local chemist made up the comr ound, which Miss Briggs took yesterday afternoon. It is supposed to have contained poison, for the lady expired in a short time in great agony. A posf-mortem ex tmination was to be made last night. _

THE ROUND TABLE CONFERENCE.—Speaking at Glasgow on Friday evening, Sit George Trevelyan said Mr. Cham- berlain had practically admitted the accuracy of hie version of the Round Table Negotiations, bat it was not in Mr. Chamberlain's nature to make an admission or a withdrawal without doing something for the purpose of paying out the person to whom he bad to apologise. Mr. Chamberlain said that Sir George Trevelyan had never remonstrated with him for the asperity of his language during the negctiatioos; but he ('il. George) had never said that he remonstrated with the hon. gentlemin. He had simply orged upon him the necessity of not losing an opportunity for reconcilia- tion.

, THE sREFFIELD MIIRDER.—Henry Hobson (52), engine tenter, charged with the murder of Ad .e Stothard, wife of a bore merchant, on Sate rday morning, was on Fliday morn- ing brought before the Sheffield stipendiary. Evidence was given that spots were found on the prisoner's trousers, coat, and vest, which the borough analyst, Mr. Allen, believed to be recent spots of human blood. The deceased's husband proved that the prisoner bad threatened him, and after other evidence the wounded servant girl Florence Mosley was examined. She positively identified the prisoner, whom she had seen three times before. John Hardy, green- grocer, who met the murderer running frem the house, also identified him.

ALLEGED POISONING OF AN TRISH LLIIY.—The inquest on Mr e Cross, wife of Surgeon-Maj w Cross, of Shandy Hall, county Cork, was resumed on Friday, at Coachford. The analysis of the viscera has been completed, and on Thurs- day Dr. Cross was placed under arrest. Dr. Coss alleged that his wife died in June of typhus fever, and a few days after the fnneral he married his governess. On Friday the courthouse was crowded. Dr. Pearson stated that the post•mortem examination showed there was a complete absence of food from the stomach and intestines, and there was no evidence whatever that the deceassd died of typhoid fever as represented by her husband. There were evidences of an irritant, and no natural cause was found to account for death. On an analysis of the gullet, stomach. intes- tines, liver, kc , he discovered white arsenic, thi - bring pre- sent in large quantities. In his opinion deceased died from poison. He found strychnine in the stomach. Dr. Cross's cminsel declined to cross-examine the witness at this inquiry.

div.head: ELECTION NEWS.
div.p: ELECTION NEWS.

The polling for the Forest of Dan Division of Gloucester- ebire for the vacancy caused hy the resignation of Mr. Thos Blake (GL), proceeded on Friday at nineteen polling sta- tions. It opened at eight o'clock amid a hsavv downpour of rain, which threatened ts return during the day, and only a few votes were recorded in the first hour. 'niers is no work at the pits and ironworks in the district for the diy. Mr. Samuelson (GL) and Mr. Wyndham (C) are the candidates. It is generally believed that there will be a very heavy poll.

div.head: GREAT FIRE INT CIIICAGG.-I2 LIVES LOST.
div.p: GREAT FIRE INT CIIICAGG.-I2 LIVES LOST.
CHICAGO, FILIDAY.—A large tukery was destroyed by fire early this morning. Two persons were suffocated and ten others were so terribly burned that they have since died.

RAILWAY ACCIDENT.-22 LABOURERS KILLED. A goods train on the Chicago and Alton Railroad on Thmsdav ran into a construction train near Bloomington, Illinois, when 22 labourers were killed, and many others were injured. GENERAL BGULANGER AND M. JULES FERRY. PA.RIS, FRILL/ay.—General Boulanger his resolved to challenge M. Ferry, on account et the speech recently de- livered by the latter at Epinal, attacking the General. The general's second bearing the challenge left Clermont-Fer- rand 3+ ettel day.

LAST NIGHT'S PARLIAMENT. HOUSE OF LORDS. The House met at four o'clock. MISCELLANEOUS.—Lord ARMsTRONG took the oath and his seat on his elevation to the peera4e.--The Bankruptcy Offices Sites Hlt was read a thial time.--In reply to Earl Delaware Earl ONSLOw said the Government were willing to give the Maltese as large a share of popular representa- tion as was conaimmt with the secntety of the fortreas.- -The Merchandise Marks Bill passed through committee, and other bills were advanced a stage. The House then adjourned. HOUSE OF COMMONS. The House met at four o'clock. QUESTIONS —Mr. C. STANNOUS, replying to Mr. Howard Vincent, hoped to be able Wore the close of the se,sion to State the course proposed to be taken with regard to the , recommendations of the Royal Commission on warlike stores.—The ilomK SECRETARY, replying to Mr. John Ellis, said he had advised strict investigation into the charges made against the police as to blackmailing. To state pub- licly what wasth be done would defeat the object in view.— Mr. JACKSON, replying to Mr. Broadhurst, said it was in- tended to introduce a bill amending certain provisions of the Friendly Societies Act this session.—Colonel KING HARINAN, replying to questions, sought to justify the pro- claiming of county Dublin under the Crimes Act. He also defended the proclamation of Ring's County, where intimi- dation prevailed.—Tbe HOME SECRETARY said he would see whether the report of the inquiry regarding the treatment of Mies Cass could be made puolic. IRISH LAND BILL—The House then went into Com- mittee on ths Irish Land Law Bill. On clause four, which provided the substitution of a written notice for the execu- tion of an ejectment. Mr. PARNELL waved the following addition to the clause Nothing in this section shall be taken or construed to restrain any landlord from proceeding with his judgment in eject- ment otherwise than as herein provided, but it is hereby enacted that where the landlord elects to, proceed by notice under this section and the tenancy of the holdings is deter- mined, the holding, or any part thereof, if re-let within fif- teen years from such determination, should be subject from and after the time of its being so let to all the provisions of the land Law Land Act, 1881, which are applicable to pre- sent tenancies."—Mr. A. BALFOUR contended that if the al- ternative processes were te be retained, it would not be rea- sonable to drive landlerds into the first method by penaliz- ing the second.—Mr. PARNELL warned the Government that if any large amount of evictions took place under the present bill it would seriously aff-ct the larger measure on land purchase promised by the Government. Mr T W RUSSEL), objected to the amendment, as it raised the /thole question of future tenants.—Mr. Dimore sup- ported the amendment, which. he said, only proposed to do an act of iustice.—After discussion, during which it was stated that the object desired by the amendment could be better carried out in clause 22, the amendment was with- drawn.—On the question that the clause as amended stand part of the Hell, Mr DitzoN congemned the clause as utterly bad, and moved is rejection.—Sir W HARCOURT condemned the clause as one to make eviction easy. He strongly objected to the manner in which the opinion of Irish members were disregarded.—Mr A PALFovn defended the clause, and denied that the opinions of Irish members were disregarded —For the clause, 143 ; against, 111. The i clause was then ordered to stand as part of the bill. [LEFT sirrirto.]

OPENING OF A NEW WELSH CHAPEL.—The opening services in connection with the new Welsh Wesleyan Chapel, Tamworth-street, Earleatown, were held on Sunuay last. The building is a neat and attractive one, and the Welsh worshippers are well pleased with its accommoda- tion and convenience. The foundation stone was laid on May 14th last, and the work has rapidly progressed under the personal supervision of Mr. Kellett, manager far Pennington, of Earlestown, who secured the contract for its erection. It finds sitting room for about 120 mrsons, and the total cost has been about £3OO. towards which sum a large amount ho been raised. Its erection in the specified time an I the excellent manner in which the work has been carried out has given every sttisfaction to the congregation and friends, and credit is due to Mr. Kellett, who has entire charge of the arrangements. At the opening setvices on Sunday the pleasant little chapel was well filed. The services throughout the day were conducted in Welsh. In the morning the preacher was the Rev. 0. L. Davies, superintendent minister of the Liverpool circuit, and in the afternoon the pelpit was Occupied by the RPV. Robert Jones, of Bangor, chairman of the North Wales District. In the evening both the rev, gentlemen named gave addresses. Collections were made at each service in aid of the building fund, and about £45 were realised.
